subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: When the Codex app-server native relay cannot be invoked, should OpenClaw treat generic before_tool_call evaluation as the authoritative equivalent security boundary, or require relay recovery while remaining fail-closed?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes a native execution approval failure from hard block to fallback, and source/tests cannot establish the repository's desired security posture for transport errors.

options.title: Require live equivalence proof
options.body: Accept fallback only after exact-head restart/drain evidence shows recovery plus preserved plugin blocking, trusted policy, loop detection, and approval prompts.

options.title: Preserve fail-closed recovery
options.body: Rework the app-server path to refresh or re-register the relay and continue blocking until the current relay can evaluate the native request.

options.title: Accept fallback by policy
options.body: Explicitly declare generic before-tool-call evaluation the supported boundary for relay-unavailable app-server approvals and add focused contract coverage.

recommendation.title: Require live equivalence proof
recommendation.body: Accept fallback only after exact-head restart/drain evidence shows recovery plus preserved plugin blocking, trusted policy, loop detection, and approval prompts.

likelyOwner.reason: The most directly relevant merged contract work established the guarded unavailable fallback behavior this PR changes.
